title: The if statement: do something only when true

visuals.title: if (marks >= 50): is the body run?

branches.label: Condition is TRUE: the body runs and prints "Congratulations, you passed!". Then the program continues.

visuals.elseLabel: Condition is FALSE: the body is skipped. Nothing is printed for this if. The program continues after it.

visuals.title: if (temperature > 35): hot day message
visuals.elseLabel: FALSE: the body is skipped, nothing extra is printed.

goal: After this you can write a one-way if statement, explain when its body runs, and avoid the brace and semicolon mistakes.
warmup: Think about the weather. IF it is raining, you take an umbrella. If it is not raining, you do nothing special and just walk out. Another one: IF your mobile balance is below Rs. 50, you buy a load. Otherwise you do nothing. There is one condition and one action that happens only when the condition is true.
definition: The if statement runs a block of code only when its condition is true. If the condition is false, the block is skipped and the program carries on with the next statement after it. The condition is an expression that gives true or false, usually made with a relational operator such as marks >= 50.
howItWorks: Slide the value and watch the decision. The computer first checks the condition inside the brackets. If it is true, it runs the statements inside the braces { }. If it is false, it jumps over them. Either way, the next line after the if block is always run.

worked.problem: If the temperature is above 35, print "It's a hot day!". Then always print "Program finished." (temperature is 38).
pseudocode: IF temperature > 35 THEN PRINT "It's a hot day!"
worked.flowchartMermaid:
flowchart TD
  A([Start]) --> B[temperature = 38]
  B --> C{temperature > 35?}
  C -- True --> D[/Print It's a hot day/]
  C -- False --> E[/Print Program finished/]
  D --> E
  E --> F([End])

sample.title: Hot day message
sample.expectedOutput:
It's a hot day!
Program finished.

explanation.text: Checks the condition. 38 > 35 is true, so the body runs.
Inside the braces: this runs only when the condition is true.
Outside the if block: this always runs.

steps.note: Is 38 > 35? Yes, the condition is true, so we enter the body.
The body runs and prints the message.
The if is over. This line runs in every case.

worked.problem: Read the marks of a student. If marks are 50 or more, print "Congratulations, you passed!". Then print "Program finished." (input: 72).
worked.flowchartMermaid:
flowchart TD
  A([Start]) --> B[/Read marks/]
  B --> C{marks >= 50?}
  C -- True --> D[/Print Congratulations/]
  C -- False --> E[/Print Program finished/]
  D --> E
  E --> F([End])

sample.title: Did the student pass?
sample.expectedOutput:
Enter marks: Congratulations, you passed!
Program finished.

explanation.text: Reads the marks typed by the user.
True when marks is 50 or more. The braces hold the code to run in that case.
Runs only if the condition is true.

steps.note: This runs after the if block.

worked.problem: A shop gives 10% discount when the total bill is Rs. 5000 or more. Read the total, apply the discount if it applies, then print the amount to pay (input: 6000).
worked.flowchartMermaid:
flowchart TD
  A([Start]) --> B[/Read total/]
  B --> C{total >= 5000?}
  C -- True --> D[discount = total / 10]
  D --> E[total = total - discount]
  C -- False --> F[/Print total/]
  E --> F
  F --> G([End])

sample.title: Discount at Rs. 5000

explanation.text: Only bills of Rs. 5000 or more get the discount.
10% of the total (integer division). Two statements need braces.
Reduces the total by the discount.
Always runs: prints the final amount.

variations.when: Normal form: braces around the body (best habit)
Body is exactly one statement; braces can be left out

variations.way: Several if statements one after another
variations.when: Each if is checked on its own, independent of the others

mistakes.error: compiles with no error, but the ; ends the if with an empty body, so "Big" is printed always
compiles, but without braces only the first cout belongs to the if; B is printed always
usually compiles with no error: it stores 5 in x and is always true

examTips: Never put a semicolon right after if (condition). It ends the if with an empty body.
The condition must be inside brackets: if (x > 5), not if x > 5.
Without braces only ONE statement belongs to the if. Use braces when you have two or more.
Show the flowchart with one diamond: True goes through the body, False skips it.
In an exam trace, write the condition's value (true/false) at each if.
romanSummary: if statement ka block sirf tab chalta hai jab condition true ho.
Agar condition false ho to block skip ho jata hai aur program agli line se chalta hai.
Condition hamesha brackets ( ) ke andar likhte hain, aur if ke foran baad semicolon nahi lagate.
Do ya zyada statements ho to braces { } zaroor lagayen.

practice.prompt: When does the body of an if statement run?
options: Only when the condition is true
Only when the condition is false
practice.answer: Only when the condition is true
practice.hint: Think of 'if it rains, take an umbrella'.
practice.explanation: The body runs only for a true condition; for false it is skipped.

practice.hint: Look at the condition: it needs something around it.
practice.explanation: The condition of an if must be inside brackets.

practice.hint: Each if is checked on its own. No endl is used.
practice.explanation: The first condition is true, so Ten is printed. The second is false, so it is skipped. Done always prints.

practice.hint: Without braces, only the first statement after the if belongs to it.
practice.explanation: n > 5 is false, so cout << "A" is skipped. cout << "B" is NOT part of the if, so B prints, then C.

practice.hint: Look carefully at the end of the if line.
practice.explanation: The semicolon is an empty body for the if. The cout line is a separate statement that always runs.

practice.prompt: Write a program that reads an integer and prints "Positive" only if it is greater than 0.
practice.explanation: One condition, one action: a one-way if.

quiz.prompt: What happens when the if condition is false?
quiz.hint: Think of the umbrella when it is not raining.
quiz.explanation: The program jumps over the body and continues after it.

quiz.prompt: Which is the correct way to write an if?
quiz.hint: Brackets are needed, a semicolon is not.
quiz.explanation: The condition goes in brackets and there is no semicolon after it.

quiz.prompt: int n = 2; if (n > 5) cout << "A"; cout << "B"; What is printed?
quiz.hint: Only the first statement belongs to the if.
quiz.explanation: The if body is skipped; cout << "B" is a separate statement and always runs.

quiz.prompt: What does the semicolon in if (x > 5); do?
options: Gives the if an empty body
quiz.answer: Gives the if an empty body
quiz.hint: The semicolon is a complete (empty) statement.
quiz.explanation: The if controls only the empty statement, so the next line always runs.
